results.content: [**Agentic AI**](https://www.usaii.org/ai-insights/agentic-ai-frameworks-vs-agentic-ai-platforms-which-is-best) is defined as intelligent systems that can independently set their goals, make decisions, and issue multi-step tasks with minimal human intervention. By integrating artificial intelligence with robotics, autonomous systems, IoT devices, and smart infrastructure, [**Physical AI**](https://www.usaii.org/ai-insights/welcome-to-physical-ai-innovation-beyond-imagination) bridges the gap between the digital domain and the physical world. As explored in USAII’s recent insights *“*[***Artificial General Intelligence (AGI): Challenges & Opportunities***](https://www.usaii.org/ai-insights/artificial-general-intelligence-challenges-and-opportunities-ahead) **Ahead,**” AGI also presents vast opportunities, from scientific discovery and automation of advanced cognitive tasks to new forms of human-AI collaboration and innovation acceleration across industries. results.title: Learning-based legged locomotion: State of the art and future perspectives
results.content: Since DRL approaches commonly require a large number of samples (trial-and-error experience with the system being controlled) to learn control policies, it is common practice to train the policies in simulation and then transfer them to the real world ([Tan et al., 2018](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/02783649241312698#bibr323-02783649241312698); [Hwangbo et al., 2019](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/02783649241312698#bibr151-02783649241312698)). In the domain of learning-based locomotion, on-policy model-free algorithms like trust region policy optimization (TRPO) ([Schulman et al., 2015](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/02783649241312698#bibr299-02783649241312698)) and proximal policy optimization (PPO) ([Schulman et al., 2017](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/02783649241312698#bibr300-02783649241312698)) are often preferred choices. One notable usage of IL in learning-based locomotion is privileged learning ([Chen et al., 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/02783649241312698#bibr49-02783649241312698)), which first learns a capable teacher policy with ground-truth information and copies the behaviors into a student policy with a realistic sensor configuration.
